record.paper_title: Infinity in string cosmology: A review through open problems
record.original_question: When anisotropies are added to tree-level string cosmologies with NS-NS fields, RR fields, or both, what asymptotic regimes occur in simple anisotropic models, which asymptotic decompositions and cancellations are possible, and can one identify lower-parameter attractor solutions that organize the full solution space of these string cosmologies?

evidence.quote:
2.3 Asymptotics of speciﬁc tree-level string actions III
The next step is to incorporate anisotropies into the asymptotic regimes and study simple anisotropic models with NS-NS and/or RR ﬁelds. There will be many decompositions of the vector ﬁeld asymptotically and there may be solutions with a smaller number of arbitrary constants which still attract other families of solutions. We expect here the phenomenon of asymptotic cancellations to occur.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider tree-level low-energy effective string actions in D spacetime dimensions of the form
  S = ∫ d^D x √(-g) e^{-φ} ( R + (∇φ)^2 - (1/12) H_{μνρ} H^{μνρ} ) + S_RR ,
where φ is the dilaton, H = dB is the field strength of the NS-NS two-form B, and S_RR denotes contributions from Ramond-Ramond p-form field strengths F_{(p+1)}, included individually or in combination with H. Restrict to spatially homogeneous, anisotropic cosmologies of Bianchi type I, with metric
  ds^2 = -dt^2 + Σ_{i=1}^{D-1} a_i(t)^2 (dx^i)^2 ,
and with φ = φ(t), and with B and F_{(p+1)} compatible with the homogeneity (so their components depend only on t).

Introduce expansion-normalized variables (Hubble rates H_i = ȧ_i/a_i, the shear σ_{ij}, the dilaton velocity, and the appropriately rescaled NS-NS and RR field strengths) so as to recast the field equations as an autonomous polynomial dynamical system on a finite-dimensional state space, and study its asymptotic behavior as t → ±∞ (or as the system approaches a singular boundary).

Address the following:

1. Classify all asymptotic regimes (equilibrium points, heteroclinic chains, and invariant boundary subsets) of this dynamical system in the cases (a) only NS-NS fields are excited, (b) only RR fields are excited, and (c) both NS-NS and RR fields are excited.

2. Determine all decompositions of the asymptotic vector field into dominant balances, and identify which "asymptotic cancellations" — situations where leading-order terms cancel forcing one to subleading orders — actually occur.

3. Identify lower-parameter attractor solutions: solutions depending on strictly fewer than the maximal number of arbitrary constants that nevertheless attract open families of full-parameter solutions in the asymptotic limit, and describe their basins of attraction.

Provide a complete answer for the simplest nontrivial anisotropic models (e.g. Bianchi I in D = 4 and D = 10 with one or two excited form fields).
artifact.status_search_result: A literature search shows partial results for restricted cases: NS-NS-only anisotropic Bianchi-I cosmologies with dilaton and B-field have known attractor and pre-Big-Bang solutions, and some D-brane / RR-driven anisotropic models have been analyzed. However, a complete classification of asymptotic regimes, dominant-balance decompositions, asymptotic cancellations, and lower-parameter attractors covering combined NS-NS + RR anisotropic tree-level string cosmologies has not been established. The full problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Recent progress in classical string cosmology
status_evidence.snippet: Review of classical string cosmology covering pre-Big-Bang and tree-level effective actions; lists open issues including detailed asymptotic structure of anisotropic models with form fields.
status_evidence.claim: Recent reviews still treat the full asymptotic classification of anisotropic NS-NS/RR string cosmologies as an open program.

status_evidence.title: Tree-level string cosmology (Phys. Rev. D 53, 4247)
status_evidence.snippet: Foundational analysis of tree-level string cosmology dynamical equations.
status_evidence.claim: Provides background framework but does not give a full classification including RR fields and anisotropic attractors.

status_evidence.title: String cosmology of the D-brane universe (Phys. Rev. D 74, 126001)
status_evidence.snippet: Studies homogeneous anisotropic cosmology driven by dilaton and antisymmetric tensor with D-branes; identifies particular attractor solutions.
status_evidence.claim: Demonstrates partial progress: attractor behavior identified in restricted NS-NS + brane settings, not the full NS-NS+RR classification.
